One summer day, when I was around 16, I was at the beach in Liguria (northern Italy) with my usual bunch of friends. And, alas, a girl I had a huge crush on.

The sea was stormy that day. Like, very bad, there were red flags all along the beach and there wasn't anyone in the water. I'm a fairly good swimmer, and a friend and I used to love diving in waves that most people wouldn't have ever dared.

Keep in mind that the Mediterranean is indeed a fairly calm sea, but it can get very nasty at times, as the scores of ships on its floor can testify. The sea floor tends to rise up fairly abruptly near the coast, which makes the waves rise up very quickly once they get close to the shore, and crush down like fists immediately after. Not the kind of wave you can surf in, as in stormy weather they just get tall, fast and violent.

Anyway, that day the waves were a bit too much, even for a stupid 16 years old who thinks he can outswim everything, and I wasn't really considering getting anywhere near the water. So I sat there, mesmerised by the spectacle of that force of nature roaring just before me, my friends doing teenager things behind me, the voice of my crush mixed with the sound of the sea.

Then, God knows what took me, I just got up, ran towards the next wave and dived under it. Honestly I don't remember why the fuck I did that. Surely I wanted to impress that girl, I can't even remember her face now. Also, you now, sixteen and a bloody idiot and whatnot. When I think about it I still ask myself why I did it.

Long story short, instead of popping out behind the first wave at a manageable distance from the next one (as I always did), and thus being able to get back before being crushed against the sea floor, I found myself right before another fucking wall of water. To avoid being rolled I had to dive underneath again, and again, and again.

Soon I found myself uncomfortably far away from the shore. Once I realised that, I tried to swim back, but I seemed to get further and further away. Also, I wasn't really sure that getting back right then was a good idea, as even at that distance I could see the foam of those giants breaking on the rocky beach, and I was pretty sure it wouldn't have been fun being under them.

So there I was, swimming just to stay afloat, scared to get back and scared to get dragged too far away.

Luckily the waves wouldn't break that far from shore, but Christ they were scary. Once on the crest I felt like I was on top of a moving mountain, from which I could see the next horrifying monster speed towards me. While in the trough between them, I would stare in horror at the incoming wall towering over me, deafening and terrifying.

After a while (no idea how long), I got pretty tired, and I started thinking I wasn't going to make it back. I went under a few times, unable to keep my head out of the passing waves, and I got even more scared.

I remember thinking "fuck, I'm seriously going to die today, this is how it happens, it's happening right now, oh fuck". The thought made me gather the last of my remaining energies, so I tried again to try and swim towards the beach. I swam only when at the top of the wave, and rested a moment while waiting for the next. Also, that part is pretty blurry now but I think the sea was being a bit less furious at that moment.

So I got close to the shore, and I got indeed slammed violently against the floor. I remember it like being rolled in a washing machine together with a few tons of rocks and pebbles. I spun so many times I lost track of where up and down where, and also what direction the next wave would come from, assuming I would be able to take a small breath before it came.

Luckily, some people who had followed the ordeal managed to drag me out of the water, all covered in blood from a gash in my head and several other minor scratches pretty much everywhere. I was like half a mile from where I had dived, but fuck it, I was so happy to feel solid ground under my feet I was actually laughing.

I have never, ever been so scared. Even now, after almost 30 years, I have nightmares where I am at sea and there are tsunamis, or huge dark waves or whatever.

The girl I meant to impress, needless to say, wasn't impressed at all. Also, lots of strangers told me to my face I was a fucking idiot, and what the fuck was I laughing for? I couldn't argue.
